newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat futures end thinly-traded session lower.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat futures end thinly-traded session lower.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower, but trading throughout the session was light and featureless.
Floor sources reported that prices drifted down during the session, possibly pressured by lower CBOT grain markets.
KCBT traders said there was a lack of bullish news on which to trade, and the light volume made it difficult to apply a reason for the selling. Many traders remained on holiday.
Floor sources said the light attendance in the pit caused a lack of liquidity making it difficult to complete trades.
Sri Lanka reportedly bought Argentine and Australian wheat early Friday, but KCBT traders said U.S. wheat was not expected to be included in the purchase.
KCBT wheat closed down 5-1/2 cents per bushel to up 1/2 cent with March off the most at $3.99-1/2 per bushel.
